claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy undergoes rapid oxidation in oxygen-rich environments at extreme temperatures.
The untreated alloy experiences oxide-scale degradation under extreme-temperature, oxygen-rich exposure.
Aluminizing can create an aluminum-enriched surface on the refractory high-entropy alloy.
An aluminum-enriched surface promotes formation of an Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be coherent and adherent.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will grow slowly.
Aluminum in the treated surface diffuses toward the exterior during high-temperature exposure.
Exterior-directed aluminum rapidly forms a protective Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
Limiting oxygen ingress reduces the oxidation rate relative to the untreated alloy.
Under approximately 1200 degrees Celsius, 1 atm air, and 100 hours of exposure, aluminizing will improve oxygen resistance by approximately two- to threefold relative to the untreated alloy.
Under the specified exposure, aluminizing will reduce oxidation-associated mass gain.
Under the specified exposure, aluminizing will produce a thinner oxide scale than that on the untreated alloy.
Under the specified exposure, aluminizing will delay oxidation-related degradation.
At 1200 degrees Celsius in air for 100 hours, the untreated alloy exhibits heavy mass gain.
At 1200 degrees Celsius in air for 100 hours, the untreated alloy forms thick, non-protective oxide scales.
The oxidation-resistance benefit depends on the Al2O3 scale remaining adherent and stable.
Scale spallation or breakdown at more severe temperatures or exposure durations will diminish the protective effect.
